newsitem.title: USA: Papers show Holocaust began in occupied Russia.
newsitem.headline: Papers show Holocaust began in occupied Russia.

text.p: Newly released documents show that more people died in the Holocaust than previously believed and prove that thousands of Jews were killed in the German invasion of Russia in 1941, a historian said on Monday.

Richard Breitman, a history professor at American University, said in a telephone interview he was writing a book based on his review of 1.3 million pages of British documents, including intelligence intercepts of German radio traffic held by the U.S. National Security Agency.
Breitman's research raises a number of issues including how many Jews and members of other groups were killed by Nazi Germany and what kept Britain from publicising the slaughter earlier in the war.

The documents showed that British intelligence was fully aware that widespread killing of Jews and others was under way in western Russia, having intercepted radio traffic in July, August and September 1941. That was a year before the infamous Nazi death camps began operating at Buchenwald and Auschwitz. German forces invaded Russia on June 22, 1941.

Some historians have long accused Britain of deliberately not releasing information about the extermination programme, which became widely known only at the end of the war in 1945, when allied troops released the inamtes of the death camps.

Breitman, who gained access to the documents after filing a request under the Freedom of Information Act, said the British managed to decode shortwave radio messages to Berlin from commanders on the Russian front. "Hitler and Himmler were following these events in Russia very closely and shortwave radio was the quickest way to tell them," he said.

He said messages to Berlin showed that the Order Police -- municipal police forces who have only recently been portrayed by some historians as playing a major role in the slaughter -- moved into western Russia to carry out the killings. Many people associate the atrocities only with elite SS units under the command of Heinrich Himmler.

Breitman said the head of the Order Police, Kurt Daluege, warned his underlings by radio on Sept. 13, 1941, to stop mentioning the number of executions they were carrying out for fear of alerting the enemy. But Breitman found a number of incriminating messages before that cutoff, including one from a field commander to Berlin headquarters in August 1941 saying "the total number of executions in territory under my jurisdiction has now exceeded 30,000."

He said it would be difficult to determine precisely how many more Jews were killed based on the new documents. "You could simply add up the numbers contained in the messages decoded, or you could extrapolate from the pace of the killings and come up with a far higher number," he said. "I suspect it would be somewhere in between."

Most historians believe 6 million Jews died in the Holocaust, although researchers have managed to verify the names of only about 3 million of the victims. In addition 9 to 10 million Gypsies, Slavs, Poles, Ukrainians, Serbs and others were exterminated.
Elan Steinberg, executive director of the World Jewish Congress, said the research shed new light on what happened in the east and refuted arguments that only the SS carried out the slaughter.
"This puts a further nail in the coffin that the SS did all the killings," he said. "The black hole in Holocaust history relates to mass killings in the east by the mobile killing squads."
